entities.summary: Richard Ernest Kunze was a physician. He came to the United States in 1854, and was graduated at the Eclectic Medical College of New York in 1868, subsequently becoming a member of the board of trustees of this institution, was president of the New York Therapeutical Association in 1880, introduced to the medical profession various drugs derived from cacti, and added greatly to the previous knowledge of medical botany. He published a series of monographs on Cactus ; Cereus Grandiflorus and Cereus bonplandi (1876); Cereus triangularis and Phyllocactus grandis (1876); Cardinal Points in the Study of Medical Botany ; and The Germination and Vitality of Seeds (1881).

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Kunze's contributions to medical botany and his introduction of cacti-derived drugs expanded knowledge in this field, particularly in North America. His publications on Cactus species helped advance the study of medical botany.
